option_description: Whether the third party holds a current, scope-relevant independent security attestation (SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001) that has been reviewed within the assessment cycle, with the consumed service explicitly in scope.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Trusted-relationship supply-chain pivot" — fires when false (no attestation, expired report, or a report whose scope excludes the consumed service), because without independent assurance the provider protects what it handles, a provider compromise can pivot inward (T1199) with no prior verification of the chain of trust.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the vendor risk file for a current independent security attestation covering the consumed service.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Vendor risk file contains a current SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001 report, reviewed within the assessment cycle, with the consumed service in scope; CIS 15.5 assessment evidence (questionnaire responses + audit results) on record

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the attestation's Trust Services Criteria coverage and that its scope/criteria genuinely match the consumed service before treating it as assurance.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AICPA Trust Services Criteria coverage confirmed (Security at minimum); gaps tracked. Per secureframe SOC 2 vs questionnaire guidance, a SOC 2 report substitutes for re-asking questionnaire items only where its scope and trust criteria match

option_description: Whether this third party is recorded in the maintained service-provider inventory with a data-sensitivity classification and a designated enterprise contact/owner.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Trusted-relationship supply-chain pivot" — fires when false (absent from inventory, or present without classification/owner), because trust granted to an uninventoried provider is unmanaged and unmonitored, so a provider compromise pivots inward unnoticed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search the service-provider inventory for an entry covering this provider with a classification and a named owner.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 15.1 inventory lists this provider with classification(s) and a designated enterprise contact; CIS 15.3 classification reflects data sensitivity, data volume, availability requirement, and applicable regulation

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the inventory entry carries a data-sensitivity classification (not just a name) so the trust is risk-rated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Entry shows data-sensitivity classification and named enterprise owner/contact; an entry missing either counts as not inventoried

option_description: Whether the executed agreement embeds security-requirement clauses and, where personal data is shared, a Data Processing Addendum (sub-processor, breach-notification, and data-location terms) is on file.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for both "Trusted-relationship supply-chain pivot" and "Excessive data exposure across the data-sharing boundary" — fires when false (no security clauses / no DPA despite PII sharing), leaving the trust relationship contractually unbounded with no breach-notification obligation to surface a provider compromise and no contractual control over shared-PII handling.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the executed contract for embedded security-requirement clauses and the documented trust relationship.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 15.4 evidence: executed agreement contains security requirement clauses; where personal data flows, a DPA is on file. NIST SA-9 trust relationship (SA-9(3)) and consistent-interests (SA-9(4)) documented

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a DPA on file names sub-processors, a breach-notification SLA, and permitted processing locations where PII is shared.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DPA on file naming sub-processors, breach-notification SLA, and permitted processing locations; aligns with GDPR Art.28-style processor obligations and the AWS-style DPA structure

option_description: Whether organizational oversight and user roles for the external service are documented and a pre-reliance risk assessment was performed and approved by the designated authority before outsourcing the function.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Trusted-relationship supply-chain pivot" — fires when false (no defined owner, no approved pre-reliance risk assessment), because the trust was extended without evaluating chain-of-trust confidence, widening the supply-chain pivot exposure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a documented pre-reliance risk assessment was approved by the designated authority before reliance, with oversight roles defined.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: NIST SA-9 base: oversight and user roles documented; SA-9(1) risk assessment performed and approved by designated personnel before outsourcing the function; chain-of-trust confidence recorded

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the approval predates the go-live / first reliance on the integration, not a retroactive sign-off.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Approval record is dated before the integration entered service; a defined owner and documented user roles are on file

option_description: Attestation that the third-party API credential resolves at runtime from a secrets manager / injected environment, never hard-coded in source or committed to the repository.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Stolen or over-scoped API credential abuse" — fires when false, because a hard-coded or committed key is directly exfiltratable and replayable (T1552) with no extra access required.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the credential resolves from a secrets manager / injected env var at runtime and is not committed, with a rotation schedule on record.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key resolves from a secrets manager / env injected at runtime, not committed; rotation schedule on record. Stripe key best-practice: never embed in code, rotate periodically, revoke on compromise

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the source tree and repo history for committed live key material.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No live secret-key material found committed in the repository (a hit indicates an insecure-stored third-party credential)

option_description: Attestation that the third-party API credential is rotated on a defined schedule and on staff offboarding.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Stolen or over-scoped API credential abuse" — fires when false, because a never-rotated credential remains valid indefinitely once stolen, removing any natural blast-radius bound (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a documented rotation schedule exists and is enforced, including the secret-manager-resolved storage best practice.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key resolves from a secrets manager / env injected at runtime, not committed; rotation schedule on record. Stripe key best-practice: never embed in code, rotate periodically, revoke on compromise

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the provider dashboard, check the active key's creation/last-rotated date against the rotation policy.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Provider dashboard > API keys / Developers > key details > Created / Last used
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active key's last-rotation date falls within the documented rotation interval; an old creation date with no rotation history indicates the control is absent

option_description: Attestation that the OAuth scopes / API-key permissions granted to the provider are constrained to the integration's actually-used endpoints.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for both "Stolen or over-scoped API credential abuse" and "Over-broad outbound token scope" — fires when false, because broad or default scopes let a stolen or misused credential act with excessive privilege across the provider API (NIST AC-6, RFC 9700 narrowest-scope).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Compare the granted scopes/permissions against the integration's actually-used endpoints for least privilege.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Granted scopes match the integration's used endpoints only; per RFC 9700 OAuth BCP, request the narrowest scope and prefer short-lived access tokens; NIST AC-6 least privilege applied to the service account

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the provider dashboard, view the key/app permission set and confirm only required resource scopes are enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Provider dashboard > API keys > Restricted key > resource permissions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Provider dashboard shows the key as a Restricted key with only required resource permissions enabled (Stripe: restricted-key scopes; not a full secret key)

option_description: Attestation that the credential is an unrestricted full-access secret key / shared account / broad basic-auth credential rather than a restricted least-privilege key or OAuth client_credentials with minimal scopes.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Stolen or over-scoped API credential abuse" — fires when true (inverted: the secure value is false), because a full-access key maximizes the blast radius when replayed (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the provider dashboard, determine whether the credential is a full/admin secret key or a restricted least-privilege key.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Provider dashboard > API keys > key type (Secret vs Restricted)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Provider dashboard shows the key as a Restricted key with only required resource permissions enabled (Stripe: restricted-key scopes; not a full secret key)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Where OAuth is used, confirm the client_credentials grant requests only minimal scopes rather than full access, and that keys authenticate clients only.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Where OAuth is used, the client_credentials grant requests only the minimal scopes; per OWASP API2 API keys authenticate clients only, never end-users, and tokens are validated for signature + expiry

option_description: Classification of the breadth of scopes/permissions granted to the third-party token, from least_privilege through full_access.
security_impact: The OR-trigger for "Over-broad outbound token scope" — fires on the insecure complement (write_all / full_access), where broad OAuth scopes / key permissions granted by default exceed the integration's need; the least-privilege baseline values stay silent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Classify the provisioned scope/permission set into one of the enum buckets against the integration's actual need.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Granted scopes match the integration's used endpoints only; per RFC 9700 OAuth BCP, request the narrowest scope and prefer short-lived access tokens; NIST AC-6 least privilege applied to the service account

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the granted scopes/permissions from the provider dashboard and map them to the closest enum value (read-only/scoped vs write-all/full).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Provider dashboard > API keys / OAuth app > granted scopes
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Provider dashboard shows the key as a Restricted key with only required resource permissions enabled (Stripe: restricted-key scopes; not a full secret key)

option_description: Age in days of the currently-active third-party API credential since its last rotation.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Stolen or over-scoped API credential abuse" — fires when greater than the 90-day rotation maximum, because a long-lived static secret stays exploitable for the full window after exfiltration (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the active credential's creation / last-rotation timestamp from the provider dashboard and compute its age in days.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Provider dashboard > API keys / Developers > key details > Created
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Creation/last-rotation date of the active key; age in days computed from today's date (e.g. 42)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check against the documented rotation schedule to confirm the key has actually been rotated within policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key resolves from a secrets manager / env injected at runtime, not committed; rotation schedule on record. Stripe key best-practice: never embed in code, rotate periodically, revoke on compromise

option_description: Attestation that a documented decommissioning process revokes the integration credential and removes access on staff departure / relationship termination.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Stolen or over-scoped API credential abuse" — fires when false, because lingering, unrevoked credentials remain an exploitable foothold after offboarding (T1078, T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the decommissioning procedure for credential-revocation records on departure / termination.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 15.7 evidence: decommissioning procedure with access-revocation records and data-destruction certification; orphaned keys/federation removed

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the NIST AC-2 account lifecycle is applied to the service/integration account.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: NIST AC-2 account-management lifecycle applied to the service/integration account: disabled and removed on relationship termination

option_description: Whether the inbound callback/webhook handler cryptographically verifies the provider's signature header (HMAC over the raw unmodified body) against the signing secret before acting on the payload, rejecting on mismatch.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or replayed inbound webhook / federation assertion" — fires when false, because the endpoint then accepts forged webhook payloads (e.g. a fake payment-success event) driving fraudulent state changes (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the handler verifies the provider signature header over the raw body against the signing secret before acting and rejects on mismatch.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handler verifies the provider signature header against the endpoint signing secret over the RAW unmodified body before acting (Stripe: Stripe-Signature header, whsec_ secret, t=/v1= scheme); rejects on mismatch

how_to_obtain.instruction: POST an unsigned forged payload to the callback endpoint and confirm it is rejected, not processed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Request without a valid signature header is rejected (401/400), not processed

option_description: Whether the inbound callback handler enforces a timestamp/replay window (validating the signed t= timestamp and rejecting stale or previously-seen events) so a once-valid signed payload cannot be replayed.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or replayed inbound webhook / federation assertion" — fires when false, because a captured legitimate webhook can then be replayed (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the handler validates the signed timestamp against a tolerance window and rejects stale / already-seen events, alongside signature verification.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handler verifies the provider signature header against the endpoint signing secret over the RAW unmodified body before acting (Stripe: Stripe-Signature header, whsec_ secret, t=/v1= scheme); rejects on mismatch

how_to_obtain.instruction: Replay a previously-captured valid webhook (or one with an old t= timestamp) and confirm it is rejected as stale.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -X POST https://app.example/webhooks/provider --data-binary @captured-event.json -H 'Stripe-Signature: <captured old t= signature>'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Replayed event with a stale timestamp is rejected (400/401); a 2xx indicates no replay window is enforced

option_description: Where the third party is an identity-federation partner, whether the relying party validates the assertion/token signature against the partner's pinned signing certificate, rejecting unsigned or wrong-signer assertions.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or replayed inbound webhook / federation assertion" — fires when false, because forged (Golden SAML) assertions are then accepted, granting unauthorized cross-federation access (T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the relying party validates the assertion signature against the partner's pinned signing certificate and rejects unsigned / wrong-signer assertions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RP validates SAML assertion signature, Issuer, AudienceRestriction, NotOnOrAfter, and recipient; signing certificate matches the federation partner. NIST 800-63C federation assurance applied

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the configuration enforces signed assertions validated against the expected IdP certificate, rejecting unsigned ones.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per OWASP SAML cheat sheet: enforce signed assertions, validate against the expected IdP cert, reject unsigned/expired assertions; prevents forged/replayed assertions

option_description: Whether the relying party validates the assertion AudienceRestriction / recipient (or OIDC aud claim) so a token minted for another service cannot be replayed against this one.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or replayed inbound webhook / federation assertion" — fires when false, because a stolen or cross-audience token then grants unauthorized cross-federation access (T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the relying party validates the AudienceRestriction / aud claim against this service's expected identifier.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RP validates SAML assertion signature, Issuer, AudienceRestriction, NotOnOrAfter, and recipient; signing certificate matches the federation partner. NIST 800-63C federation assurance applied

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the SAML/OIDC config for the configured expected audience/entity-id and that assertions for other audiences are rejected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per OWASP SAML cheat sheet: enforce signed assertions, validate against the expected IdP cert, reject unsigned/expired assertions; prevents forged/replayed assertions

option_description: Whether the relying party validates the assertion Issuer (or OIDC iss claim) against the expected federation partner identifier.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or replayed inbound webhook / federation assertion" — fires when false, because an assertion from an unexpected or attacker-controlled issuer can then be accepted (T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the relying party validates the assertion Issuer / iss claim against the expected federation partner identifier.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RP validates SAML assertion signature, Issuer, AudienceRestriction, NotOnOrAfter, and recipient; signing certificate matches the federation partner. NIST 800-63C federation assurance applied

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the federation config for the pinned expected issuer/entity-id value the RP checks against.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per OWASP SAML cheat sheet: enforce signed assertions, validate against the expected IdP cert, reject unsigned/expired assertions; prevents forged/replayed assertions

option_description: Whether the relying party enforces assertion/token freshness (NotOnOrAfter / exp) so an expired or replayed assertion is rejected.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or replayed inbound webhook / federation assertion" — fires when false, because expired or replayed assertions are then honored (T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the relying party enforces NotOnOrAfter / exp freshness and rejects expired assertions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RP validates SAML assertion signature, Issuer, AudienceRestriction, NotOnOrAfter, and recipient; signing certificate matches the federation partner. NIST 800-63C federation assurance applied

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check that the config rejects expired assertions (and that clock-skew tolerance is bounded), per the OWASP SAML guidance.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per OWASP SAML cheat sheet: enforce signed assertions, validate against the expected IdP cert, reject unsigned/expired assertions; prevents forged/replayed assertions

option_description: Whether the callback endpoint restricts source traffic to the provider's published IP egress ranges as defense-in-depth alongside (not instead of) signature verification.
security_impact: Supporting context for "Forged or replayed inbound webhook / federation assertion" — it strengthens the defense layer but the cryptographic verification facets are the load-bearing triggers; an open callback endpoint widens the forged/replayed inbound surface.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a network/WAF rule allowlists the provider's documented webhook egress IP ranges to the callback path.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Network/WAF rule allowlists the provider's documented webhook egress IP ranges to the callback path; combined with (not instead of) signature verification

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an IP outside the provider's published ranges, POST to the callback path and confirm it is blocked at the network layer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connection from a non-allowlisted source is refused/dropped (connection reset or 403 at the edge) before reaching the handler

option_description: Whether outbound calls to the third-party endpoint are made over TLS (https://) rather than plaintext (http://).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Man-in-the-middle on the integration channel" — fires when false, because plaintext calls expose shared data and credentials to interception/alteration in transit (T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open a TLS connection to the provider endpoint and confirm a valid certificate chain and TLS handshake (i.e. the channel is https/TLS, not plaintext).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Valid, in-date certificate chain to the provider's hostname; handshake negotiates TLS 1.2 or 1.3

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the integration client config / base URL to confirm the provider endpoint is configured as https:// rather than http://.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured provider base URL uses the https:// scheme; no plaintext http:// endpoint in client config

option_description: Whether the integration client validates the provider's TLS server certificate chain and hostname (verify=on / rejectUnauthorized:true) rather than disabling verification.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Man-in-the-middle on the integration channel" — fires when false, because disabled validation lets a man-in-the-middle present a forged certificate and silently intercept or alter the channel (T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the client code/config to confirm cert verification is NOT disabled (no verify=False / rejectUnauthorized:false / curl -k).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Client code does NOT disable cert verification (no verify=False / rejectUnauthorized:false / curl -k); ASVS V9 requires authenticated, validated TLS for all external connections

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the provider presents a valid, in-date certificate chain for its hostname (a precondition for verification to be meaningful).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Valid, in-date certificate chain to the provider's hostname; handshake negotiates TLS 1.2 or 1.3

option_description: Minimum TLS protocol version negotiated on the channel to the third-party provider (workspace-canonical TLS-version enum).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Man-in-the-middle on the integration channel" — fires on the insecure value tls1_0_or_tls1_1_or_sslv3_accepted, which is downgrade-vulnerable and broken, enabling interception/alteration in transit (T1557); tls1_2_or_higher stays silent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the protocols/ciphers the channel will negotiate to determine the lowest accepted TLS version.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLS 1.2/1.3 with strong ciphers offered; SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 absent

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the handshake negotiates TLS 1.2+ on the connection to the provider.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Valid, in-date certificate chain to the provider's hostname; handshake negotiates TLS 1.2 or 1.3

option_description: Whether only the minimum necessary data (especially PII) is shared with the provider, with sensitive fields excluded or tokenized where not functionally required.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Excessive data exposure across the data-sharing boundary" — fires when false, because full records / unnecessary PII leaving the boundary widen the blast radius of a provider breach and create compliance exposure (T1213).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run a data-flow review of what fields leave the boundary to the provider and confirm only required fields are shared.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Data-flow review shows only required fields leave the boundary; GDPR Art.5 data-minimisation honored; PII categories shared are documented and justified

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm shared PII follows NIST SP 800-122 confidentiality controls (classification, minimization, masking where feasible).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: PII handling for shared data follows NIST SP 800-122 confidentiality controls (classification, minimization, masking where feasible)

option_description: Whether the provider's sub-processor list is disclosed and has been reviewed and accepted.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Excessive data exposure across the data-sharing boundary" — fires when false, because undisclosed sub-processors extend data exposure to fourth parties outside the org's control (T1213).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the DPA sub-processor list is disclosed and reviewed against the data-location requirement.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: NIST SA-9(5) processing/storage/service-location restriction documented; DPA sub-processor list reviewed; CSA CCM data-residency / supply-chain controls mapped

how_to_obtain.instruction: Evaluate the disclosed sub-processor posture against CSA CCM supply-chain / data-privacy domains.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CSA Cloud Controls Matrix domains (Supply Chain Management, Data Security & Privacy) used to evaluate the provider's residency and sub-processor posture

option_description: Whether the provider's processing/storage/service location is constrained per requirement (restricted_documented / restricted_undocumented / unrestricted).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Excessive data exposure across the data-sharing boundary" — fires on the insecure value 'unrestricted', where data may leave the required jurisdiction, creating GDPR/PII residency exposure outside the org's control (T1213).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the provider's processing/storage location is contractually restricted and documented per NIST SA-9(5).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: NIST SA-9(5) processing/storage/service-location restriction documented; DPA sub-processor list reviewed; CSA CCM data-residency / supply-chain controls mapped

how_to_obtain.instruction: Map the provider's residency posture to CSA CCM data-residency controls and classify into the enum bucket.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CSA Cloud Controls Matrix domains (Supply Chain Management, Data Security & Privacy) used to evaluate the provider's residency and sub-processor posture

option_description: Whether outbound calls to the third-party provider are bounded by explicit connect/read timeouts.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Availability dependency / cascading outage" — fires when false, because an unbounded call to a stalled provider blocks dependent threads and cascades the outage (T1499).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the client configures connect/read timeouts (alongside a circuit breaker and fallback path).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Client configures connect/read timeouts and a CircuitBreaker (failureRateThreshold, slidingWindow, waitDurationInOpenState) with a fallback path; per Resilience4j config a tripped breaker fails fast instead of cascading

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the integration client config for explicit non-default connect and read timeout values.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Client config sets explicit connect/read timeouts (e.g. 2s/5s) rather than relying on unbounded library defaults

option_description: Whether calls to the third-party provider are wrapped in a circuit breaker (failure-rate threshold, sliding window, open-state wait) that trips to fail fast on sustained provider failure.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Availability dependency / cascading outage" — fires when false, because a hard single-vendor dependency with no breaker lets a provider outage or rate-limit cascade into the dependent system (T1499).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm provider calls are wrapped in a circuit breaker with a failure-rate threshold, sliding window, and open-state behavior.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Client configures connect/read timeouts and a CircuitBreaker (failureRateThreshold, slidingWindow, waitDurationInOpenState) with a fallback path; per Resilience4j config a tripped breaker fails fast instead of cascading

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the provider's availability-requirement classification and SLA used to size the breaker thresholds.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SLA on record; CIS 15.3 availability-requirement classification used to size resilience; single-vendor lock-in risk noted

option_description: Whether a fallback / graceful-degradation path exists so the dependent system continues in a reduced mode when the third-party provider is unavailable.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Availability dependency / cascading outage" — fires when false, because with no fallback a provider outage or SLA breach halts the dependent system (T1499).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a fallback path exists that lets the dependent system continue in a reduced mode when the provider is unavailable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Client configures connect/read timeouts and a CircuitBreaker (failureRateThreshold, slidingWindow, waitDurationInOpenState) with a fallback path; per Resilience4j config a tripped breaker fails fast instead of cascading

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the SLA and availability classification to confirm the degraded mode meets the dependent system's continuity requirement.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SLA on record; CIS 15.3 availability-requirement classification used to size resilience; single-vendor lock-in risk noted

option_description: Whether outbound calls to and inbound callbacks from the third party are logged with correlation IDs and retained per policy.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unmonitored third-party interactions" — fires when false, because unlogged interactions blind anomaly detection and incident response, so credential abuse, forged callbacks, or provider compromise go undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect logs for third-party request/response metadata with correlation IDs and retention.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Logs show third-party request/response metadata (endpoint, status, latency, correlation id) with Authorization/keys redacted; CIS 15.6 continuous monitoring evidence present

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the log-retention policy covers third-party interaction logs for the required window.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Retention policy on record covering third-party interaction logs; logs present for the full required retention window

option_description: Whether credentials (Authorization headers, API keys, tokens) are redacted from third-party interaction logs.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unmonitored third-party interactions" — fires when false, because secrets logged in cleartext (CWE-532) turn the log store into a credential-leak source.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search third-party interaction logs for any cleartext secret material.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No secret material in logs (guard against CWE-532 sensitive-info-in-log); OWASP logging guidance followed

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm Authorization headers, API keys, and tokens appear redacted/masked in the captured interaction logs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Logs show third-party request/response metadata (endpoint, status, latency, correlation id) with Authorization/keys redacted; CIS 15.6 continuous monitoring evidence present

option_description: Whether the provider's security advisories, release notes, and breach/dark-web signals are continuously monitored.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unmonitored third-party interactions" — fires when false, because provider incidents and known-vulnerable integration code then go unnoticed (CIS 15.6 continuous monitoring).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm SCA shows the provider SDK on a supported version and that provider advisories/release notes and breach signals are monitored.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SCA shows the provider SDK on a supported, non-vulnerable version (OWASP A06 vulnerable/outdated components); CIS 15.4 monitoring includes provider release notes / dark-web signals

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify a named owner/process subscribes to and triages the provider's advisory and breach feeds on a defined cadence.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented continuous-monitoring process with a named owner ingesting provider advisories, release notes, and breach/dark-web signals
